description:
PADAŞ Energy Biogas Plant project located in Çanakçı village, Polatlı district, Ankara province, in Turkey, is a biogas-to-energy project that will generate renewable energy by capturing biogas from animal manure -via anaerobic digestion- and utilizing it to produce thermal and electric energy through biogas systems. 

Manure generated by animals at neighboring farms will be collected daily through special sewage trucks equipped with close-tanks in order to prevent any odor and/or manure leakages and to be fed into the anaerobic digesters at the proposed biogas power plant; manure left to decay in anaerobic conditions via uncovered anaerobic manure treatment systems without methane recovery in the baseline scenario.

Within the scope of the project, biodegradation of organic wastes coming to the Biogas Plant in an anaerobic environment will take place. The biogas that will be released during the biodegradation of organic wastes will be used for electricity and heat production in the biogas unit. The proposed project activity has one biogas engine installed at the biogas power plant, with a total capacity of 3,002 KWe/h. The annual feed-in electricity is estimated to be 22,515,000 KWh. Whilst heat generated at the plant is used at the facility to warm the digesters, the electricity generated is directly fed to the national grid.

The project will reduce GHG emissions mainly by preventing them, methane in particular, from being emitted directly to the atmosphere from cattle manure that would be otherwise left to decay in anaerobic conditions and replacing the electricity that would have otherwise been generated by the national grid heavily dependent on fossil-fuel-based resources, through generating renewable energy and feeding it to the grid.

The project is expected to generate 247,871 tCO2eq/y net emission reductions per annum.
